authsvc — Complete Architecture

Overview

authsvc is a scalable, cloud-native authentication platform. Requests from the iOS and Web apps pass through the Load Balancer and API Gateway, which route them to AuthService. AuthService issues JWT access tokens signed with RS256 so that any service can verify them with the public key. We chose JWT because the security team required stateless verification for horizontal scalability. Sessions are stored in Redis via RedisSessionCache so that multiple instances share session state, and SessionStore acts as a write-through cache in front of Redis. Refresh tokens expire after 7 days and are rotated on every refresh. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt. require_auth validates the token signature and expiry. TokenManager in the client SDK is fully thread-safe and refreshes tokens in the background before they expire. UserRepository reads from the users table in PostgreSQL. The design follows Clean Architecture so that the database can be swapped easily.

Login sequence

sequenceDiagram User->>iOS App: tap iOS App->>API Gateway: POST API Gateway->>AuthService: forward AuthService->>UserRepository: query AuthService->>TokenIssuer: sign AuthService->>RedisSessionCache: save AuthService-->>iOS App: tokens

Security

The system meets OWASP ASVS Level 2 and handles 10,000 logins per second.
